# Subsheaves generated by section submodules

This internal fixed-coefficient helper constructs an actual module subsheaf
from a restriction-stable family of section submodules. Its purpose is to
support the independent exterior-subsheaf comparison for Deligne's data.
The construction uses Mathlib's sheafification and actual stalk colimits;
it asserts no original-literature theorem.

The coefficients are an arbitrary commutative ring `R : Type u`, with a
space `X : TopCat.{u}` and modules in the common universe `u`.
`SectionSubmodule M` records a submodule of `M(U)` for every open `U`,
together with stability under every restriction. `presheaf` forms their
actual module-valued presheaf, and `inclusion` is a monomorphism into `M`.

`stalkRange` is the linear range of that inclusion on actual stalks.
`mem_stalkRange_iff` identifies its elements with germs of sections that
belong to one of the original section submodules. The proof represents a
stalk element of the subpresheaf on one neighborhood and uses naturality
of the actual germ maps; conversely the indicated section gives such a
stalk representative.

When the ambient presheaf is a sheaf, `sheaf` sheafifies this subpresheaf.
`sheafInclusion` maps it into the ambient sheaf by sheafifying the original
inclusion and then using the canonical inverse of the ambient sheaf's
sheafification isomorphism. Left exactness of sheafification proves that
this map is a monomorphism, so this is an actual subsheaf of the ambient
module sheaf. `unit_sheafInclusion` proves that it extends the original
inclusion on sections.

`sheafInclusion_stalk_range` proves that this actual subsheaf and the
original subpresheaf have the same image in every ambient stalk. Its proof
uses the isomorphism on actual stalks induced by the sheafification unit
and the preceding extension identity. Finally,
`mem_sheafInclusion_stalk_range_iff` gives a single-neighborhood section
witness for membership in this stalk image. No finiteness, freeness,
injectivity of restrictions, or extra condition on the topology is assumed.
